name: eitc
question: Using law as of June 30, 2025, calculate the 2025 EITC amount only. Filing status is joint; EITC eligibility is established. The complete qualifying-child roster consists of exactly two named qualifying children, whose classifications are established. Earned income is $32,000; established AGI is $35,000. Investment income consists of $1,000 interest and $2,000 net capital gain; there is no tax-exempt interest, rent/royalty excess or passive excess; the year is not short, and no §32(k) disallowance period applies. These are explicit calculation inputs, not facts you should infer. Use the published 2025 joint threshold and show the phaseout result.
scope: Credit amount with eligibility and qualifying-child classifications explicitly established; not an eligibility adjudication or a whole tax return.

name: foreign-tax-limit
question: Using law as of June 30, 2025, calculate the foreign tax credit for 2025 in one established basket: US citizen with an established effective §901 credit election; eligible foreign income tax paid is $28,000; US tax before credit is $30,000; foreign-source taxable income for §904 is $120,000 and worldwide taxable income for §904 is $160,000. No §911 benefits, loss recapture, carryovers, treaty resourcing or additional adjustments apply. Compute the limitation and allowed credit, not residence or wage-source classification.
scope: One established income basket, no §911 exclusion, carryovers, loss recapture, treaty resourcing or other adjustments. Income source and taxes have already been determined.

name: wash-sale-loss
question: On March 1, 2025, a taxpayer sells a fully matched stock lot for $6,000 with adjusted basis $8,000, realizing a stated $2,000 loss. On March 15 they buy the same quantity of substantially identical stock for $5,000. Quantity matching and substantial identity are established. Using law as of June 30, 2025, compute the §1091 disallowed loss and replacement basis. Do not add the loss to the old basis instead of the replacement acquisition cost.
scope: Fully matched equal quantities and established substantially-identical stock; partial-lot allocation and alternative wash-sale transactions are outside this case.
